findings.problem: status is pub String; any string value including "", "sent", "garbage", or "deleted" is representable
findings.failure_mode: Caller sets status to an arbitrary string that bypasses domain invariants; no state machine enforces valid transitions
findings.fix: Replace with an enum: enum SampleStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }. Remove is_sent and is_validated booleans.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a lifecycle boolean that allows inconsistent states (both false, both true, or sent without validated)
findings.failure_mode: SampleWorkflow can be both not-validated and sent simultaneously, or neither validated nor sent but not in a proper initial state. No transition ordering is enforced.
findings.fix: Encode lifecycle as typestate transitions in the Status enum variants: enum SampleStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at: Instant } }. Remove is_validated field.

findings.problem: is_sent: bool is a lifecycle boolean redundant with status:String but independently mutable, allowing desync
findings.failure_mode: Caller can set is_sent=true while status="pending", creating contradictory internal state that no invariant checks catch at compile time
findings.fix: Remove is_sent. Let the Status enum variant carry sent-related data. If sent_at is needed, store it in the Sent variant.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a bare optional lifecycle field; it can be None while is_sent=true or status="sent", or Some while not sent
findings.failure_mode: Option is a dumb container that doesn't enforce semantic coupling. sent_at_epoch_ms can be Some(123) on a Pending workflow, or None on a Sent workflow.
findings.fix: Move sent timestamp into the enum variant that owns it: Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }. Remove the bare Option field.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive; no domain semantics, no uniqueness guarantee, no format validation
findings.failure_mode: Empty string, whitespace-only, or non-ASCII IDs are accepted with no validation. id can be confused with other string fields at call sites.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype: pub struct SampleId(String). Provide a smart constructor that rejects empty/whitespace IDs and returns a typed error.

findings.problem: All fields are pub with no smart constructor; every combination of values is constructible and no invariant is enforced at construction time
findings.failure_mode: A caller can instantiate SampleWorkflow with status="", is_validated=true, is_sent=false, sent_at_epoch_ms=None — an invalid state with no compile-time or runtime protection
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide a smart constructor `SampleWorkflow::new(id: SampleId) -> Result<SampleWorkflow, NewError>` that sets valid initial state. Remove pub visibility from all fields.

findings.problem: mark_sent directly mutates status and booleans, bypassing any typestate transition logic. It can be called on any SampleWorkflow regardless of prior state
findings.failure_mode: A workflow can be marked sent without ever being validated. mark_sent can be called multiple times. There is no pre-condition check or transition guard.
findings.fix: Replace with a method on the typestate enum: impl SampleStatus { fn transition_to_sent(self, now: u64) -> Result<SampleStatus, TransitionError> }. Callers must hold a validated state to reach Sent.

findings.problem: No smart constructor exists for SampleWorkflow; fields are directly assignable via pub visibility
findings.failure_mode: Validation cannot happen at construction time. Hostile inputs (empty id, invalid status strings) pass through unchecked.
findings.fix: Private fields + pub fn new(id: SampleId) -> Result<Self, CreationError> with validation logic inside.

findings.problem: mark_sent returns SampleWorkflow with no error type; all state mutations are infallible by construction
findings.failure_mode: If a transition should fail (e.g., not in Validated state), there is no error type to return. The API pretends every transition always succeeds.
findings.fix: Return Result<SampleWorkflow, TransitionError> where TransitionError::NotValidated, TransitionError::AlreadySent, etc.

findings.problem: No benchmark exists. The module has no performance claims documented, but no baseline measurement is available for any future optimization.
findings.failure_mode: Future refactors (typestate enums, smart constructors) introduce indirection without knowing the cost baseline.
findings.fix: Add a criterion or minitrace benchmark for mark_sent on a representative SampleWorkflow before making changes.

missing_evidence: no benchmark for mark_sent or SampleWorkflow construction
no profiler data showing allocation patterns for String fields
no command output from cargo clippy or cargo test
no allocation/Vec evidence for to_string() on status field in mark_sent (allocates every call)
residual_risk: The struct permits arbitrary invalid states at compile time. All six fields are pub, making the typestate model completely unenforceable. mark_sent is an infallible free function that mutates state without guards. Every String field allocates on construction and on every mark_sent call. This is the sample pattern the review task is named after — invalid state is trivially representable.
